scope: Bounded Lab audit of the first query-selection repair only: candidate af32eb6b0b vs test-only baseline a385e46e60 (product base 442f6f38 / 0.3.296) in worktree Lab-remaining-delivery-verification-20260910. Covered the story_list handler diff (story-query.ts), docs/CLI.md disclosure, packages/main/tests/story-list-selection.test.mjs, experiments/remaining-delivery-verification/query-read-probe.mjs, and output/story-list-red-green evidence (finding-and-scope.json, native-red/green logs, native-status.json, timing-plan.json, timing-results.json, four instrumented witnesses, timing-attempt1). Independently re-ran the single authorized test. PASS means bounded Lab mechanism verification plus exploratory REVIEW-only query timing; NOT main integration, NOT product release, NOT closure of the six delivery-time claims, NOT proof that hours-long Story delivery is solved. git diff was denied by the sandbox in both literal and -C forms; I compared output/story-list-red-green/baseline-checkout/packages/main/src/handlers/story-query.ts against the worktree copy, which spans the same two commits. main untouched; no Story JSON, lease, gate or worktree mutated.

findings.problem: The newly added doc sentence says --active "includes REVIEW along with the other non-terminal lifecycle phases", and the in-code comment says active excludes only DONE/DISCARDED/IDEA. Per core/lifecycle-registry.ts:79-93, TERMINAL_LIFECYCLE_PHASES is DONE/DISCARDED only and META is a registered non-terminal (NON_ACTIVE) phase, but META is absent from NON_TERMINAL_PHASES, so a META story is dropped from --active with no omitted count (the filtered path returns a bare array with no _phases/_omittedTerminal accounting). The exclusion itself is pre-existing (baseline ACTIVE_PHASES at baseline-checkout story-query.ts:538-546 was also an allowlist omitting META), so this is not a regression; the inaccurate generalization is new with this change. META also has no fixture in the test (test file :18), so the behavior is unasserted.
findings.correction: Replace the generalization with the explicit included phase set (or derive it from an exported lifecycle-registry constant) and state that IDEA and META are excluded as non-active phases; add a META fixture to the phases array so the intended exclusion is pinned.

findings.problem: Selection now runs on the workspace-resolved projection for every story, so the decisive correctness boundary is a story whose root phase is terminal but whose residual worktree reports a non-terminal phase. The fixtures contain only the opposite shape (B-linked: root INIT_CHECK, worktree REVIEW). The terminal-phase guard that keeps a DONE/DISCARDED story from being re-admitted to --active by a stale worktree is therefore never exercised, and a future regression in resolveStoryWorkspace would pass all ten controls.
findings.correction: Add a fixture (e.g. B-residual) with root phase DONE and a linked worktree projecting DEV, and assert it is absent from story_list({active:true}) and that none of its checklist/bug/evidence/metrics reads occur.

findings.problem: The disclosed behavior change is that an IntentAmendmentIntegrityError raised by an excluded Story's checklist no longer aborts a filtered listing (docs/CLI.md:70-73, "A filtered listing is not an integrity audit of excluded Stories"). The test pins only the positive direction (a selected corrupt row still throws). The complementary contract - excluded corrupt rows must NOT throw - is asserted in prose only, so the disclosed weakening is documented but not test-bound.
findings.correction: Add a control that sets corruptId to an excluded id (e.g. 'B-DONE') and asserts story_list({phase:'REVIEW'}) returns normally without throwing, alongside the existing propagate case.

findings.problem: The three pair orders are red/green, green/red, red/green, so 2 of 3 pairs are red-first on one shared host with n=3 and warm filesystem cache; order is not balanced. Separately, the REVIEW timing case selects only 3 rows out of ~390 stories, i.e. close to the maximum-benefit selectivity for this fix, and no equal-output timing exists for --active at all (correctly, since REVIEW omission is being fixed). The stored summary field observedReductionPercent: 66.16 is therefore not representative of typical filtered use. All runs are correctly uninstrumented (instrumented:false), digests are byte-identical across all six runs, and validInputSnapshot is true over 1418 inputs, so the direction of the effect is credible.
findings.correction: Record the order imbalance and the 3-row selectivity in the timing-results scope/summary text, and require observedReductionPercent to be quoted only as "exploratory, REVIEW-only, order-imbalanced, best-case selectivity" - never as a general query speedup.

findings.problem: Rows keep a mainPhase field when the linked worktree phase diverges from the root phase, and it flows into the brief projection (story-query.ts:70). The test asserts B-linked's phase is REVIEW but never asserts mainPhase === 'INIT_CHECK', so that part of the preserved output shape is unpinned for the case the fix specifically touches.
findings.correction: Extend the existing linked-worktree control to also assert mainPhase === 'INIT_CHECK' on the B-linked row.

limitations: git diff a385e46e60..af32eb6b0b was denied by the sandbox in both the literal form (cwd is not a git repository) and the git -C form; before/after comparison was done by reading output/story-list-red-green/baseline-checkout/packages/main/src/handlers/story-query.ts against the worktree copy. That checkout is itself Lab-produced evidence, so its fidelity to commit a385e46e60 is assumed, not independently verified by me.

Only the single authorized test was executed (node packages/main/tests/story-list-selection.test.mjs); no broader suite, no CLI end-to-end run, no lifecycle or gate exercise. My GREEN reproduction confirms the handler mechanism, not product integration.

The real-data witnesses and timing runs were read as recorded artifacts; I did not re-execute query-read-probe.mjs, so their elapsed times and detail counts are taken as reported (their internal consistency - identical resultSha256, empty changedDuringProbe, matching dist paths - did check out).

Timing evidence is three pairs on one shared host and is exploratory only. I did not attempt to reproduce or statistically validate it, and the active-case pair 1 overlap with native GREEN is disclosed in the artifacts rather than independently confirmed by me.

JSON inputs were read bounded and contain path digests rather than Story bodies, so I could not verify the semantic content of the production stores the probes read - only that no probed input digest changed during the campaign.
I did not audit whether these two query defects are causally related to hours-long Story delivery; nothing in this evidence set addresses that, and the artifacts correctly disclaim it.
summary: PASS for bounded Lab mechanism verification plus exploratory REVIEW-only query timing. The reproduction is valid and the root causes are correctly attributed: baseline story-query.ts:538-546 defines a local ACTIVE_PHASES allowlist without REVIEW and filters at :601-605 only after the hydration map, while the candidate resolves projections at :548 and filters at :549-553 before hydrating selected rows. The 9-vs-7 delta is fully explained by REVIEW omission (B-REVIEW plus B-linked, which projects to REVIEW); baseline already filtered on the projected phase, so there is no undisclosed third behavior change. Before/after is real, not stubbed: native-status.json records RED at a385e46e60 (exit 1, observedActive 7, activeDetailCalls 1248) and GREEN at af32eb6b0b (exit 0, 9 / 36 / review 8), and instrumented witnesses against the real file-backed repository corroborate on production stores with detailCalls 1548 to 164 (active) and 1548 to 12 (review), changedDuringProbe empty on all four. I independently re-ran the authorized test and observed STORY_LIST_SELECTION_GREEN with 10/10 controls passing. Invariants hold: the dashboard branch is unreachable under a filter (:604), so global _phases, _dashboard, _bugSummary and _omittedTerminal still cover the full population (asserted at test :53-54); mutual-exclusion refusal, brief/full shape, withdrawn counts and evidence fields, and linked-worktree authority via readStoryProjection (:415-429, terminalPhaseGuard true) are all preserved. Skipped details are not an integrity gate and docs/CLI.md:68-73 discloses that a filtered listing is not an integrity audit. Timing is honestly scoped: all six runs are uninstrumented, RED and GREEN dist paths are distinct and correct, all six resultSha256 values are identical, validInputSnapshot is true over 1418 digests with a post-campaign re-hash at run-timing.py:19, the attempt-1 invalidation is preserved without row deletion, and no percentage is claimed for active. The five issues are documentation precision and test-coverage gaps, not defects in the shipped logic; F1 is a pre-existing exclusion newly described inaccurately rather than a regression. None of this evidence supports any claim about hours-long Story delivery, and the artifacts correctly disclaim it as limits[0]. This is the first bounded query repair, not closure of the six delivery-time claims and not a basis for main integration or release.
